summary: Unexpected edge probe / warmup metering line on invoice after model canary swap
description: Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected invoice line labeled 'edge-cache-probe' and 'tool-invoke:warmup' that consumed ~120k tokens and was billed at reserved rates after a model canary alias swap. Impact: BrightLens sees a $4,200 unplanned line on their monthly invoice; finance team is asking for explanation and reversal. Environment: Dedicated cluster (BrightLens dedicated pool), production, us-west region. Suspected correlation with a canary alias swap that happened 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC during a routine model variant rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer performed a canary alias swap from redwood/llama-3b-8bit -> redwood/llama-3b-quantized at 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC.
2) Immediately after swap, automatic edge warmup probes were triggered by regional edge agents to populate KV caches and run prefix warmup heuristics.
3) Probes appear to have been routed through the hosted fallback path due to transient capacity pressure in the dedicated pool, but were billed at the customer's reserved rate in billing backfill.
4) Invoice shows 'edge-cache-probe' and 'tool-invoke:warmup' line items for 2026-03-10 02:14-02:30 UTC totaling ~120,345 tokens billed at reserved/dedicated rates.
5) Customer claims they did not intentionally run any batch or embed jobs during that window.

router logs 2026-03-10T02:14:58Z: dedicated pool saturated, fallback triggered to hosted pool; fallback policy: use-compatible-variant
kv-cache metrics 2026-03-10: high prefix miss rates observed 02:10-02:20 UTC, edge warmup triggered by autoscaler heuristics
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:00 - Initial triage by Support (Sofia): identified invoice line and matched backfill job. Notified Billing Eng and SRE.

2026-03-11 11:20 - Billing Eng (Anika) noted tokens were attached to reserved rate_id despite router showing hosted-fallback path. Hypothesis: backfill pipeline reconciled postbacks by org tag and applied reserved billing tag during merge step.

2026-03-11 15:45 - SRE (Evan) reproduced scenario in staging: canary swap triggers edge warmup probes that may traverse fallback path under saturation. Repro shows probes emitted with probe tag but postback processor normalizes tag -> reserved when org has reserved_pool:true. Edge agent postbacks contained origin tag that should have prevented reserved rate application but metadata lost during async pipeline handoff.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Found reconciliation code path in metering-service (metering-reconcile.go) that overwrites route metadata when postback arrives with warmup tag; code path added in commit github.com/redwood-inference/metering-service@commit=ab3c5f2 to prioritize reserved mapping for dedicated orgs. That commit didn't account for edge-origin probes which should be treated as free warmup (no-charge) per edge warmup policy.
2026-03-12 13:00 - Confirmed produced tokens in backfill are genuine probe tokens (short sequences with warmup prefix). Customer tests confirm no manual traffic.
comments: Support - Sofia Martinez (2026-03-11 09:12): Hi BrightLens team — we're investigating the unexpected line on your invoice. I've cross-referenced the invoice id INV-2026-03-10-BL and located a backfill job that posted tokens. We'll loop in engineering and billing. (Assigned to Evan)

Customer - Aaron Lee, BrightLens Finance (2026-03-11 10:03): Thanks Sofia. The line is marked 'edge-cache-probe' on the invoice and our finance team needs a reversal if it's a warmup probe. We did a canary swap but did not launch any traffic. Please advise ETA.

Billing Eng - Anika Rao (2026-03-11 11:45): I've pulled billing-backfill logs. Backfill applied rate_id reserved-us-west-1 for the org. Need metering team to confirm classification of these postbacks (probe vs real usage).

SRE - Evan Burke (2026-03-11 16:05): Reproduced behavior in staging. Postback pipeline normalizes routing metadata and reserved flag is overriding 'probe' tag. Sketching fix: preserve edge-origin or warmup tag through reconciliation step. Will open PR and attach link once ready.

Support - Sofia Martinez (2026-03-12 14:12): Update for BrightLens: engineering identified the reconciliation bug that caused warmup probes to be billed. We're prioritizing a fix and will submit a provisional credit for the charged amount while code change is validated.
Customer - Aaron Lee (2026-03-12 15:03): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm when credit appears and whether similar events can be suppressed in future rollouts.
resolution: Root cause: metering reconciliation logic overwritten probe/origin metadata for postbacks coming from edge warmup probes, causing reserved rate assignment. Fix: metering-service PR #1423 updates reconciliation to preserve 'edge-warmup'/'probe' tags and enforce zero-charge policy for probe tokens. Action taken: provisional credit of $4,200 issued to BrightLens (credit memo CM-2026-03-13-BL) pending finalized billing backfill correction. Deployed hotfix to staging 2026-03-13 and scheduled production rollout 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC after smoke tests. Follow-ups: add e2e test to prevent metadata overwrite, update runbook to include warmup postback detection, and create alert for large warmup token spikes tied to canary swaps.
